HFSS Eigenmode, in Ansys AEDT, finds a model's resonant modes and returns
each mode's frequency in GHz and its Q, as HFSS computes them from the
model's materials and boundaries. It needs no ports. SCGSim builds the 3D
model from the plan, the same model Palace meshes, and AEDT imports it into an
empty Eigenmode design.

This page prepares the run for the CPW coupon of
[Prepare a coplanar waveguide for AEDT](aedt-cpw-inputs.qmd). This repository
holds no recorded result of it. When the run returns,
`resolve_results(handoff.run_dir).physics_results()` gives one row per mode,
with the keys `mode`, `frequency_ghz` and `q_factor`.

## Prepare the run {#prepare-the-run}

Run this in the Python session where you made `snapshot`. It needs SCGSim
with its `aedt-epr` extra; it writes the run folder without opening AEDT.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import EigenmodeRunControl, EigenmodeSim

AEDT_VERSION = "2024.2"  # Choose explicitly: 2023.2 or 2024.2.
sim = EigenmodeSim(modeling="thin_film", aedt_version=AEDT_VERSION)
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/public-cpw-eigenmode"))
sim.set_eigenmode(
    project_name="public_cpw_eigenmode",
    design_name="CpwFiniteGroundEigenmode",
    run_control=EigenmodeRunControl(
        setup_name="Setup1", minimum_frequency_ghz=3.0, num_modes=2,
        maximum_passes=6, maximum_delta_frequency_percent=5.0,
    ),
)
handoff = sim.prepare_handoff()
print(handoff.spec_path, handoff.archive_path)
```

What the inputs mean:

- `modeling="thin_film"` builds each metal film as a sheet on its face;
  `"solid"` builds it as a solid of the film's thickness, here 100 nm of
  aluminium. [Choose the geometric approximation](../concepts/model-and-numerics.qmd#choose-the-geometric-approximation)
  explains the difference.
- `aedt_version` is the AEDT release the run will use; the solver computer
  needs exactly that release.
- `EigenmodeRunControl` is HFSS's own search and refinement: the two lowest
  modes above 3 GHz, and up to six adaptive passes, which stop once the mode
  frequencies change by at most 5 % between passes. Choose these for your
  model; [Convergence and reports](convergence-and-reports.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use)
  says what the returned convergence status does and does not tell you.
- The materials come from the plan's records, and HFSS's Region, the box of
  empty space it solves in, is the plan's vacuum region. HFSS gives its faces
  Perfect H, the condition Palace's Eigenmode solver also uses at the outer
  faces of its vacuum region.
- `prepare_handoff()` writes the run folder: the model, the request
  `aedt_spec.json`, the script `run_aedt.sh`, and an archive of the folder.

## Check, run and read {#check-run-and-read}

`EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, modeling="thin_film")`, given the plan
before `prepare()`, checks without AEDT that the model builds and can be
imported ([Check a layout](check-a-layout.qmd#aedt-eigenmode-check)).

Run the folder on a computer with AEDT
([Run a prepared model](run-elsewhere.qmd#aedt-execute-the-prepared-package-locally)),
bring it back whole, and read it with `resolve_results`
([Convergence and reports](convergence-and-reports.qmd#aedt-read-the-sealed-family-evidence)).
The report keeps HFSS's convergence status and the change between its last
passes next to the frequencies
([HFSS convergence reference](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#hfss-convergence-observations)).

## Loss and participation {#loss-and-participation}

This run reports frequency and Q only. To see how a mode's energy is shared
among the surfaces, the substrate and a junction, and what loss that implies,
add an EPR request to the same simulation: the
[flip-chip Xmon example](xmon/aedt.qmd) shows it. A port sheet can also carry
a linear R, L or C, declared on the plan as a `LumpedElement`
([Lumped elements](../reference/specs/geometry-plan.qmd#lumped-elements));
this coupon has no port sheet.
